checks.reference_match: Where Sol is visible, compare the COMPLETE original mascot at a similar size: silhouette, tip/lobes, red/orange/cream contour paths and widths, face/eye proportions and limbs. Do not pass a generic flame character. Where Sol is off-screen, compare the planned setting/props and approved frame pair without requiring him. Keep user design approval separate. Allow the latest requested small action-driven body/flame wobble; judge identity by recognizable compact design, coherent colored layers and settled endpoints, rather than requiring a rigid silhouette at every intermediate pose.
checks.eyes: Keep the normal open-eye design as the original navy #1C2447 ovals, with reference shape, size, low placement and close spacing. A brief natural blink may close and reopen both eyes, returning promptly to those original ovals. Keep the face attached to the body. Intentional scripted gaze shifts may move the original ovals coherently as a pair inside the face; preserve their normal design, size and spacing. No whites, highlights, extra pupils, unrelated expressive eye morphs, winks or facial-feature drift. No independent face slide/rotation, neck or body reshaping to fake a separate head turn.
checks.flame_and_limbs: Preserve the recognizable original flame design, red/orange/cream layer relationships, reference compact form and stubby limb lengths/attachment points. Allow small coordinated body/tip/lobe flex and soft follow-through tied to the main action, settling to reference endpoint proportions. Do not reject that requested bounce as a deformation by itself. Reject inflated or remodeled anatomy, independent layer slippage, uncontrolled stretching, new limbs or a different mascot. Keep feet supported unless a step/hop is scripted. Latest size clarification: Allow tiny, sparse, brief matte painted flame flicks as secondary accents near Sol. Keep them much smaller than the eyes and subordinate to the pose. Reduce eye-sized droplets, bulbous orange-centered flares and frequent paired sprays. Preserve the main filled mascot, original lobes and coherent color layers; no holes, major lobe loss or realistic glowing fire effects.
checks.framing_and_props: Match the active scene first/last crops, camera, required character/prop counts and physical attachments. Apply only episode-specific requirements; an earlier episode does not supply mandatory props for a new story.
checks.contacts_and_action: Give every Sol pose transition a visible soft spring into the new pose, with a body bounce, overlapping tip/lobe follow-through and one brief controlled rebound that damps into the approved ending. Keep movements connected and flowing, with compact proportions and normal eyes intact. Face and filled flame layers move together. Establish attention to the fixed above-camera Narrator before his first word, then maintain it with gentle body/tip/lobe listening idle throughout the turn. No unrelated windup, repeated arm gestures, large bounce loops, unplanned hops or camera movement. Preserve short arm lengths and correct prop contact. The Sol bounce does not apply to human hands, props or mechanisms.
checks.mechanical_direction: Inspect consecutive real frames for the planned direction, rigid connections when present, and causal order of physical events. Do not infer correct movement or causality from a prompt, label, endpoint or successful decode.
checks.object_continuity: Maintain the identity and count of planned objects. A tracking mark, when present, stays attached to the same object and cannot jump, multiply or fade to fake movement. Fire may flicker or fuel may glow only as the approved action requires. Anchor actual fire to its ignition/fuel contact; any animated local lighting follows the two-frame cadence without unplanned whole-scene brightness pulsing. A transient painted effect must disappear completely when the shot requires it. Tiny secondary flicks are allowed by the latest user preference; distinguish these from oversized body chunks or core silhouette damage. Assess small secondary accents by bounce coupling as well as size/frequency; a tiny bounce-timed flick is intentional, while a persistent spray during settled listening is not.
checks.start_end_states: The actual first/last footage frames match the user-approved stills and the required resulting pose/mechanism state.
checks.performance_and_timing: Inspect actual source-frame pairs on final 30 fps timeline: each pose/painted state unchanged for two frames, 15 pose updates per second at normal speed; longer holds use complete pairs. Apply to Sol, visible human hands, moving props, flames and animated local lighting. Background and painted surface texture stay stable. Reject interpolation, blending, optical-flow smoothing and motion blur concealing steps. Check source cadence before smooth editorial transforms, then final playback/crops. Verify planned action and ending hold against actual voice timestamps; no default Narrator face turn. Sol may be absent. Judge small bouncy body/flame follow-through as intended Sol performance under the latest user clarification. It must be connected to the action, readable on twos and settled at the approved end; a brief natural blink is permitted; unrelated eye morphs, prolonged squinting and facial sliding remain failures. During visible Narrator turns, maintain above-camera gaze and gentle listening idle throughout; that requested idle is intentional, not an unrequested sway. Latest user preference requires visible flowing bounce into each Sol pose, with overlapping tip/lobe follow-through and a controlled rebound; do not reject this requested performance as an unrequested overshoot. Verify body-led above-camera attention rather than eye squish. Latest explicit direction: tiny secondary flicks accompany only intentional pose-bounce peaks/follow-through and fade as the pose settles. Quiet listening idle retains attached tip motion without fresh emissions; distinguish the separate wood fire.
checks.clean_footage: No unintended text, logos, props, narrator on screen, audio or other generation artifacts. Inspect all frames, not only the endpoints. Do not label every tiny painted tip accent an artifact. Assess flame effect size/frequency under the latest preference; large intrusive droplets remain a concern.
checks.painted_art_style: Visible soft gouache-like brushwork, layered color, subtle paper texture and expressive painted shapes cover Sol, props and environment consistently. Forms use light/color without inked outlines. Compare the selected graphic references. A smooth logo-like mascot with only a grain overlay fails even if its geometry is correct. Preserve the source character and clear mechanical contacts through the paint.
checks.script_and_narrator_attention: Read the actual complete script/storyboard and the bound per-scene dialogue/attention context, not only the video prompt. Match every spoken turn to the visible beat. Whenever Narrator speaks and Sol is visible, establish his gaze UP to the fixed above-camera voice before the first word and maintain it through the whole turn, with gentle coherent flame/body listening idle and no repeated arm gestures. Intentional paired eye-gaze adjustment is allowed while preserving the normal oval design, size, navy fill and spacing; no unmotivated feature drift or separate head. Compare actual voice cues/recordings when bound; otherwise label speech timing provisional and do not claim final synchronization. For Sol-off-screen cutaways, verify the mechanism follows the scripted explanation without inventing an invisible gaze. Evidence must include the actual script, script-context JSON and chronological/detail frames at relevant times.

review_rules: A technical probe or contact-sheet extraction is preparation, never a visual approval.
The user must see and explicitly approve BOTH first and last stills before video generation. The generator cannot approve them on the user's behalf.
A dedicated reviewer inspects actual evidence independently of generation. Every required check needs pass, fail or uncertain with evidence.
Fail, uncertain, missing evidence, missing user frame approval or a changed input blocks production approval.
Reviewing a clip does not authorize another paid generation. Preserve rejected takes.
Character geometry and painted art style must each pass. Approval of one does not establish the other or approve the complete frame pair.
Record frame-index/timestamp evidence for exact two-frame cadence, facial anchoring and hand-prop contact. Prompt wording or 30 fps metadata alone does not prove these checks passed.

Latest user direction supersedes the earlier rigid-body/no-bounce default: allow small coherent movement-triggered Sol wobble, but preserve original eyes, stubby anatomy, settled endpoints and approved soft paint. Historical rejections retain their original contracts.

Latest user clarification: allow a brief natural blink that returns to the original open navy oval design. Model preference is Omni Flash 1.2 after the comparison. Preserve material observations, but do not apply the superseded blanket no-blink rule.

Every review must bind the actual script/storyboard and available voice-cue/audio sources. A pass requires script plus actual timeline evidence for script_and_narrator_attention; a changed script, cue file or recording invalidates prior decisions. Never infer speech timing from silent media.

User approved the displayed02/05 body-tilt still pairs and requested flowing bouncy pose transitions. Still acceptance does not prove upward attention, listening idle or dialogue timing in generated clips; inspect those with script/timeline evidence.

Latest user feedback accepts subtle little flame accents and dislikes oversized emissions. Historical all-detached-piece rejections retain their original policy; current reviews distinguish tiny secondary flicks from large drops and main-body damage.
